stories.title: Next.js Ships Out-of-Band Patch for Two Critical RCE Flaws in Caching and SVG Processing
stories.summary: Next.js released an out-of-band security update on October 14 that fixes two critical flaws allowing unauthenticated remote code execution, along with a high-severity denial-of-service flaw. One code-execution flaw is in React Server Components, and the other in librsvg, the open-source library Next.js uses through the sharp package to handle SVG images. The fixes are in
stories.explanation: Next.js released an emergency security patch on October 14 to fix two critical flaws that allow attackers to run malicious code on servers without needing a password. These flaws existed in how the framework handles caching and processes SVG image files. Defenders need to immediately update Next.js to the patched version and review their deployment logs to check if these flaws were exploited before patching.

stories.title: Critical PwnEscape Linux Kernel Vulnerability Lets Guest VMs Read Host Memory
stories.summary: A newly disclosed critical flaw in the Linux kernel allows code inside a virtual machine to read memory on the host computer it runs on. A researcher demonstrated the leak against Vercel's live cloud sandboxes, and Vercel confirmed it. The flaw, now tracked as CVE-2026-99999 and nicknamed PwnEscape, is in the Linux kernel's networking code, not in any one cloud's setup, so it reaches the shared
stories.explanation: A critical flaw in the Linux kernel allows code running inside a virtual machine to read private data stored in the host computer's memory, breaking the isolation that should separate them. This is serious because cloud providers use virtual machines to isolate different customers' workloads from each other, so this flaw could expose one customer's data to another. Defenders need to patch their Linux kernels, review who has access to run virtual machines, and monitor for suspicious memory-reading activity.

stories.title: Hackers exploit Collabora RCE flaw to backdoor Nextcloud servers
stories.summary: Threat actors are exploiting a critical command execution flaw, now tracked as CVE-2026-110447, in the Collabora Online - Built-in CODE Server app (richdocumentscode) for Nextcloud.
stories.explanation: Attackers are actively exploiting a critical flaw (CVE-2026-110447) in the Collabora Online application that lets them run arbitrary commands on Nextcloud servers. Nextcloud is popular file-sharing and collaboration software, so compromised servers can lead to data theft or loss. Defenders should immediately update the richdocumentscode app, disable it if updates aren't available, and check server logs for signs of exploitation.

stories.title: Palo Alto Networks warns of PAN-OS RCE flaw exploited in attacks
stories.summary: Palo Alto Networks has released security updates for a high-severity PAN-OS RCE zero-day, tracked as CVE-2026-0322, that has been exploited in attacks targeting firewalls.
stories.explanation: Palo Alto Networks discovered a high-severity flaw in PAN-OS (their firewall software) that allows remote code execution, and attackers are already exploiting it in the wild. Firewalls are critical security devices, so compromising them gives attackers control over all network traffic flowing through them. Defenders must apply Palo Alto's security patches immediately and monitor firewall logs for suspicious activity.

stories.title: BeyondTrust patches zero-day exploited in attacks since August
stories.summary: BeyondTrust warned customers on Thursday to patch a critical flaw in its Remote Support (RS) that has been exploited in zero-day attacks since late August.
stories.explanation: BeyondTrust discovered that a critical flaw in its Remote Support product has been actively exploited by attackers since August, before a patch was publicly available (this is called a zero-day attack). Remote Support software is used to manage and access computers remotely, so compromising it gives attackers direct access to customer systems. Defenders need to patch immediately, review access logs from August onward for suspicious connections, and check if their systems were compromised.

stories.title: Drupal Patches Critical Field UI Flaw With Unauthenticated RCE Path via Contributed Modules
stories.summary: Drupal core has a critical flaw in its Field UI module that could let an attacker run code on the site's server, and fixes were shipped on October 14 in Drupal 11.4.10, 11.3.19, and 10.6.19. An attacker cannot reach the flaw through core alone, the Drupal Security Team said in its advisory. Several exploit paths exist through contributed modules, and at least one known path needs no login.
stories.explanation: Drupal released security patches on October 14 for a critical flaw in its Field UI module that allows unauthenticated attackers to run code on vulnerable websites. The flaw cannot be exploited through Drupal core alone—attackers need certain add-on modules installed—but this still affects many real-world sites. Defenders must update Drupal to the patched versions and review which contributed modules are installed on their sites.

stories.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploited BeyondTrust Zero-Day to Take Over Remote Support Servers
stories.summary: The China-nexus cyber espionage group tracked as Armory Castle (previously UNC5221 or Warp Panda) exploited a newly disclosed security flaw in BeyondTrust Remote Support (formerly Bomgar) as a zero-day in late August 2026. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-102764 (CVSS score: 9.3), is a case of improper origin validation in an internal messaging component that could be exploited by a
stories.explanation: A China-linked hacking group called Armory Castle exploited a critical flaw (CVE-2026-102764) in BeyondTrust Remote Support in August 2026 before the company disclosed or patched it. The attackers gained control of customers' remote support servers, which typically have high-level access to corporate networks. Defenders need to assume their BeyondTrust systems may have been compromised, conduct forensic investigations of activity since August, patch immediately, and reset credentials for accounts that used those servers.

stories.title: CenterPoint Energy Data Breach Impacts 1 Million Texans
stories.summary: Personal information such as names, addresses, Social Security numbers, and driver’s license numbers was compromised.
stories.explanation: CenterPoint Energy, a major utility company in Texas, suffered a data breach exposing sensitive personal information (names, addresses, Social Security numbers, driver's licenses) for about 1 million people. This kind of personal data is valuable to criminals for identity theft and fraud. Defenders should monitor breach notification sites, individuals should watch for suspicious credit activity, and companies should implement stronger data protection controls like encryption and access restrictions.

cves.name: ISC BIND Data Processing Errors Vulnerability
cves.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
cves.explanation: CVE-2015-5477 is a flaw in ISC BIND, a widely-used DNS server software, that allows attackers to cause errors in how data is processed and potentially crash the service. DNS is critical infrastructure that translates website names to IP addresses, so disrupting it affects internet availability. Defenders should have patched this years ago if it's still running, but if legacy systems still use old BIND versions, they need urgent updates or network segmentation to isolate them.

Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
cves.explanation: CVE-2015-3306 is a flaw in ProFTPD, a file-transfer server software, that improperly controls who can access files. An attacker with limited permissions might be able to access files they shouldn't, or an unauthenticated attacker might gain access to restricted areas. Defenders should update ProFTPD, review file permissions and access controls, and disable the service if it's not actively needed.

cves.explanation: CVE-2016-3081 is a command-injection flaw in Apache Struts, a popular framework for building web applications, that allows attackers to execute arbitrary system commands. If a web application built with vulnerable Struts is exploited, the attacker gets the same privileges as the web server process. Defenders should patch Apache Struts immediately, disable or isolate affected applications until patched, and review application logs for signs of exploitation.

cves.explanation: CVE-2026-76519 is a flaw in Cisco Secure Email Gateway's malware protection feature that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to write arbitrary files to the server's operating system. Email gateways are often trusted security devices positioned between the internet and internal networks, so compromising them gives attackers a foothold to attack internal systems. Defenders must patch this immediately, restrict network access to the email gateway's management interface, and monitor for suspicious file-write activity.

cves.name: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS Code Injection Vulnerability
cves.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. cves.explanation: CVE-2026-0322 is a remote code execution flaw in Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS that allows an authenticated attacker (someone with valid login credentials) with network access to run arbitrary code with root privileges on the firewall. Root privileges mean complete control of the firewall. Defenders should apply the patch immediately, implement strong authentication (multi-factor authentication), restrict network access to the management interface to trusted administrators only, and review logs for unauthorized access attempts.
